a.title: Abstract 747: A new class of DNA alkylating indolino-benzodiazepine agents (BIAs) linked with a DNA binding moiety for use with antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new class of compounds that can damage a specific type of molecule in cells, and compares their effectiveness to a similar but less effective class of compounds. It also predicts that these new compounds can be used to improve the therapeutic index of a treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of structure-activity relationship studies and experiments to identify and modify compounds that can damage the target molecule. They then tested these modified compounds in various cell lines and found that they were highly effective.

descriptions.problem: A molecule is designed to bind selectively to a specific cellular target and deliver a cytotoxic payload to cells expressing that target, with potency and specificity tuned through structural modifications.
descriptions.approach: A scaffold is engineered to bind a target site with high affinity, and its structure is modified to enhance binding strength and stability. Linkage to a targeting agent is achieved through chemically defined connections, preserving activity while enabling selective delivery.

b.title: Chemical constituents and cytotoxicity of Lepidotrigona ventralis propolis

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the chemical composition of a substance collected from a specific insect, and compares its effects on a particular type of cell. It aims to identify which compounds in the substance are most likely to harm or help these cells.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of laboratory tests to identify the individual compounds present in the substance. They then tested these compounds on a specific type of cell to see which ones were most effective at stopping its growth.

descriptions.problem: The activity of a natural mixture is assessed by measuring its effect on a specific type of human cell under laboratory conditions, identifying which components strongly inhibit cell growth.
descriptions.approach: A set of chemical substances is separated from a complex biological sample, identified using spectral analysis, and tested for their ability to suppress cell proliferation, with results reported as concentration levels that produce a defined biological response.

a.title: Phytochemical Analysis of Extractive Substances Extracted by Different Methods from the Underground Part of Aconitum Septentrionale L., and the Development of Cream-Gels Based on Them

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the composition of certain compounds in plant parts, compares the amounts of these compounds in different plant parts, and optimizes the process of isolating these compounds from the plant parts. It uses data from the plant parts' physical properties and the amounts of compounds found in them.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of physical analysis and sequential processing to isolate the compounds from the plant parts. They compare the results of different isolation methods and develop a formula for creating a new product based on the isolated compounds.

descriptions.problem: The relative abundance of specific molecular compounds is measured across different processing conditions, and the resulting formulations are evaluated for consistency and performance in delivering a desired therapeutic effect.
descriptions.approach: Plant material is processed under varying time and temperature regimes to yield different compound profiles. The resulting mixtures are combined with a base to form a stable, deliverable form, and their physical and functional properties are systematically assessed.

b.title: ВИВЧЕННЯ ТЕХНОЛОГІЧНИХ ПАРАМЕТРІВ ОТРИМАННЯ ЦЕЛЬЗІАНОВОЇ ТА СЛАВСОНІТОВОЇ КЕРАМІКИ ЗА ОДНОСТАДІЙНОЮ ТЕХНОЛОГІЄЮ

descriptions.problem: This work aims to optimise the properties of ceramic materials by adjusting their composition and processing conditions. It estimates the required properties of the materials and compares them to the existing ones.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of theoretical calculations and experimental tests to study the effects of different additives on the properties of the materials. They follow a procedure that involves synthesizing the necessary phases from raw materials and adjusting the processing conditions to achieve the desired properties.

descriptions.problem: The process determines how changes in a material's composition and processing conditions affect the resulting microstructure and physical performance, especially in achieving a dense, uniform structure with minimal defects.
descriptions.approach: A set of controlled conditions is varied systematically, and the resulting material properties are measured. Additives are introduced to influence phase development, and the outcomes are analyzed to identify optimal conditions for structural integrity and consistency.

a.title: LACTOSE TOLERANCE AND RISK OF MULTIFACTORIAL DISEASES ON THE EXAMPLE OF GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT AND BONE TISSUEPATHOLOGIES.

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between a person's ability to process a certain food and their risk of developing multiple health issues, such as weakened immune system and organ damage. It also compares this relationship across different ethnic groups.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used data from various websites to analyze the connection between a person's tolerance for a specific food and their risk of developing multiple health issues. They used statistical tests to identify patterns and correlations in the data.

descriptions.problem: A statistical relationship is estimated between an inherited metabolic trait and two health outcomes: the frequency of a specific adverse event and the rate of mortality from a related condition across diverse populations.
descriptions.approach: Data from global health records are analyzed using distribution tests and rank-based correlation to identify patterns. The strength and direction of association are quantified and used to inform preventive strategies based on individual genetic and dietary profiles.

b.title: Hypomagnesemia and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the frequency of a certain condition in a population compared to a healthy group, and identifies factors that contribute to this condition. It also predicts the risk of developing a related condition based on the presence of this condition.
descriptions.approach: The study uses data from a population to identify the relationship between a specific nutrient and the risk of developing a related condition. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and comparison to draw conclusions about the relationship.

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine the relationship between serum magnesium levels and the development of adverse cardiac outcomes, including arrhythmias and structural heart changes, in individuals with metabolic dysfunction.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model integrates longitudinal biomarker measurements, medication history, and gut microbial indicators to predict the likelihood of adverse cardiac events based on baseline and changing magnesium concentrations over time.

a.title: Study of Serum Calcium and Magnesium Levels in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients.

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the levels of two essential minerals in people with a specific health condition, and compares these levels to those in people who are generally healthy. It aims to explain why these minerals are important for overall health.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a non-random sampling method to select participants, and then measured the levels of these minerals in their blood. They used a statistical test to compare the results between the two groups.

descriptions.problem: A pattern of physiological markers is measured in individuals with a chronic metabolic condition and compared to a group of individuals without the condition to determine if differences exist and whether those differences are statistically significant.
descriptions.approach: A set of numerical values is collected from each individual and grouped by condition. A statistical test is applied to assess whether the average values differ significantly between the two groups, using a predefined threshold for significance.

b.title: Can Hibiscus Sabdariffa Decrease Blood Pressure in Menopause Women with Hypertension?

descriptions.problem: This research aims to determine the effect of a certain substance on the pressure of a fluid in the body of women who experience a certain condition, which is known to cause the fluid pressure to rise. The researchers estimate that this substance may help reduce the fluid pressure.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a simple experiment with two groups, one that received the substance and one that did not, and compared the results to see if the substance had an effect. They used a statistical test to determine if the difference in pressure was significant.

descriptions.problem: A change in a physiological parameter is assessed over time in a group exposed to a treatment and a group not exposed, using repeated measurements to determine if the treatment induces a statistically significant shift.
descriptions.approach: Two groups are assigned a standard care and one receives an extract-based intervention. Measurements are taken before and after the intervention period, and differences are compared using statistical testing to evaluate the treatment's effect.

a.title: A modified relay-race algorithm for floorplanning in PCB and IC design

descriptions.problem: This work optimizes the arrangement of complex components in a design, aiming to minimize the physical area required. It estimates the best solution by searching through a vast number of possible configurations.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves using a modified procedure to guide the search, which is based on a rule that balances the quality of solutions with the speed of the search process. The modified procedure is compared to other methods to determine its effectiveness.

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to arrange a set of components on a two-dimensional surface to minimize the total area occupied, while respecting constraints on component placement and connectivity.
descriptions.approach: A dynamic, parallel process is used where multiple candidate arrangements are evaluated and refined iteratively. Each component's position is updated based on local improvements and global consistency checks across iterations.

b.title: An asynchronous P system with a DPLL algorithm for solving a satisfiability problem

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of steps required to find a solution to a complex problem, and compares it to the number of steps required by other methods. It predicts the efficiency of a proposed algorithm for finding solutions to a specific type of problem.
descriptions.approach: The algorithm uses a set of rules to find a solution to the problem, and it can work in parallel or sequentially. The approach involves applying the rules in a specific order to find a solution that satisfies the conditions of the problem.

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to determine whether a set of logical constraints can be simultaneously satisfied by assigning truth values to a finite set of variables.
descriptions.approach: It processes the constraints in parallel using a rule-based mechanism that iteratively refines candidate assignments, reducing the search space through systematic elimination of inconsistent configurations.

a.title: Expert System of Pest Diagnosis in Passion Fruit Plants using the Bayes Theorem Method

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the likelihood of a pest being present on a certain type of object, based on characteristics of the object and the pest. It predicts the most likely pest and provides countermeasures.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a mathematical model to calculate the probability of a pest being present, based on evidence from the object. It follows a procedure of calculating probabilities and making decisions based on those probabilities.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the likelihood of a specific condition in a crop based on observed symptoms and environmental factors, comparing how well different hypotheses explain the available data.
descriptions.approach: The system evaluates each possible cause by updating the probability of a hypothesis as new observations are input, using a rule that adjusts confidence based on how consistent the evidence is with each potential explanation.

b.title: Some Pertinent Issues for Interstellar Panspermia Raised after the Discovery of 1I/‘Oumuamua

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the origin of a mysterious object from another star system, compares it to other objects, and optimizes the likelihood of life being transferred between systems. It also explains the nature of the object and the possibility of life transfer.
descriptions.approach: The researchers review various hypotheses about the object's origin, using observations and evidence from multiple objects. They use a process of elimination and falsifiability to determine the most plausible explanation.

descriptions.problem: A hypothesis about the origin of an observed object is evaluated based on its consistency with available observations and the potential for biological material to survive and transfer between systems.
descriptions.approach: Multiple origin scenarios are considered, with only one being testable through direct observation. The most plausible scenario is selected if it aligns with all observed features and allows for a mechanism by which biological material could be transported.

a.title: The Role of Wnt and BMP Signaling in Vertebrate Ocular Development and Disease

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the importance of specific proteins in regulating the growth and shape of a particular organ, and compares their effects on different types of cells within that organ. It also predicts the consequences of genetic mutations that affect those proteins.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of experiments and data analysis to investigate the role of these proteins in the organ's development. They tested the effects of genetic mutations on the organ's growth and shape, and compared the results to understand the underlying mechanisms.

descriptions.problem: A system detects and quantifies how disruptions in signaling pathways affect the shape and development of a sensory structure, particularly when regional gene expression patterns are misaligned.
descriptions.approach: A computational model simulates interactions between inhibitory and stimulatory signals across a developing tissue, adjusting gene activity based on local signal concentration to predict structural outcomes and identify mutations that disrupt balance.

b.title: PEG‐23 glyceryl distearate, a multifunctional skin‐supporting material, upregulates the expression of factors associated with epidermal barrier and hydration

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a material on the health and appearance of a critical organ, comparing its impact on the organ's protective functions and water retention. It predicts the material's role in maintaining the organ's homeostasis and optimizes its potential applications.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of laboratory experiments and 3D models to investigate the material's effects on the organ's cells and structure, analyzing gene expression and protein levels to understand its mechanisms.

descriptions.problem: A substance is tested to determine its effect on the expression of genes linked to barrier integrity and water retention in living tissue cultures that mimic real-world tissue structure.
descriptions.approach: The substance is applied to cells and tissue models, and gene activity is measured over time. The effect is evaluated by comparing gene expression levels with and without the substance, and by blocking a key regulatory pathway to assess its influence on downstream molecular responses.

a.subfield: Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health
a.title: The Relationship Between Nutritional Status and The Incidence of Dysmenorrhea in Adolescent Women

descriptions.problem: This study aims to understand the connection between a person's overall health and a common problem experienced by many during their monthly cycle. It estimates the relationship between this health aspect and the problem, and it compares the results to determine if there is a significant link.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a method that involves looking at a snapshot of a group of people to see if there is a relationship between their overall health and the problem. They analyzed the data using a statistical test to determine if the results are significant.

descriptions.problem: A statistical relationship is estimated between an individual's daily dietary balance and the frequency of menstrual discomfort, using self-reported data from a group of adolescents.
descriptions.approach: Data is collected through structured questionnaires, then analyzed using a chi-square test to determine if differences in discomfort levels are significantly linked to dietary balance, with a threshold of 5% for statistical significance.

b.title: Study of Serum Calcium and Magnesium Levels in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients.

descriptions.problem: This study estimates the levels of two essential minerals in people with a specific health condition, and compares these levels to those in people who are generally healthy. It aims to explain why these minerals are important for overall health.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a non-random sampling method to select participants, and then measured the levels of these minerals in their blood. They used a statistical test to compare the results between the two groups.

descriptions.problem: A pattern of physiological markers is measured in individuals with a chronic metabolic condition and compared to a group of individuals without the condition to determine if differences exist and whether those differences are statistically significant.
descriptions.approach: A set of numerical values is collected from each individual and grouped by condition. A statistical test is applied to assess whether the average values differ significantly between the two groups, using a predefined threshold for significance.

a.title: Uncialamycin-based antibody–drug conjugates: Unique enediyne ADCs exhibiting bystander killing effect

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new type of compound that kills cells, and compares it to a control. It predicts how well the compound will work in different situations, and optimizes its design to make it more effective.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a combination of chemical reactions and experiments to create and test the compound. They follow a procedure that involves creating the compound, testing its effects on cells, and adjusting its design to make it more effective and selective.

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to deliver a potent cytotoxic payload selectively to cells expressing a specific surface marker, with the ability to kill neighboring cells that do not express the marker.
descriptions.approach: A payload is attached to a targeting molecule via a bond that can be broken under specific conditions. The system is evaluated for its ability to kill cells in a microenvironment where only a subset of cells express the target.

b.title: Tumor-associated macrophages and cancer metastasis

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the role of certain cells in helping other cells spread and grow, and how this affects the body's ability to fight off these cells. It compares the effects of these cells to the body's response to these cells.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use data from studies to understand how these cells work together to create an environment that helps these cells survive and spread. They follow a procedure that involves analyzing the data to identify patterns and relationships between the cells and the body's response.

descriptions.problem: A system's behavior under varying conditions is inferred from observed interactions and environmental signals, with focus on how dynamic shifts in cellular states influence long-term outcomes and response to external interventions.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks state transitions in response to stimuli, using feedback loops to simulate how persistent signals drive persistent changes in function and behavior over time.

a.title: Mapping intertidal macrophytes in fjords in Southwest Greenland using Sentinel-2 imagery

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the distribution of certain types of underwater plants in coastal areas with limited access and monitoring. It predicts the extent of these plants in different regions and compares the results to understand the impact of certain environmental factors.
descriptions.approach: The study uses satellite images to identify and measure the area of these underwater plants. It follows a procedure that involves analyzing the images, applying certain rules to detect the plants, and then comparing the results to understand the impact of environmental factors.

descriptions.problem: A spatial pattern of surface cover is estimated from high-resolution images taken at different times, where the cover is visible only under specific environmental conditions, such as low water levels or calm runoff.
descriptions.approach: A model computes a surface reflectance index from image bands, then applies a threshold to detect patches of cover. Detected patches are spatially aggregated and analyzed for size and location, with results adjusted for environmental disturbances like water movement or sediment input.

b.title: Deep learning based deep-sea automatic image enhancement and animal species classification

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the quality of low-quality images of underwater creatures and classifies them into species. It compares the results to original, unenhanced images and optimizes the classification accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The approach uses a complex computer model to generate improved images from raw images, and then uses another model to classify the improved images into species. The model follows a procedure of training on a dataset, generating enhanced images, and then classifying the enhanced images into species.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the type of organism in underwater footage from low-quality visual inputs, using patterns in pixel intensity and spatial structure to assign labels with high confidence.
descriptions.approach: A neural network processes raw visual data by learning to adjust brightness, contrast, and texture to improve clarity, then classifies each frame by recognizing consistent patterns across repeated image sequences.

a.title: Treatment options for necrobiosis lipoidica: a systematic review

descriptions.problem: This work aims to collect and compare information on various methods used to help a rare, skin condition that causes collagen degeneration. It estimates the effectiveness of different methods and identifies the most promising ones.
descriptions.approach: The researchers searched for studies on various methods used to help this condition, and then analyzed the results to identify the most effective methods. They looked at case reports and series, but wanted more randomized controlled trials to compare the effectiveness of different methods.

descriptions.problem: A set of interventions is evaluated based on their outcomes in individual or group cases, with emphasis on effectiveness and reported results across diverse patient experiences.
descriptions.approach: A structured search of published accounts is conducted, filtering only those that describe both an intervention and a follow-up outcome. Evidence is compiled and summarized by type of intervention and patient response rate.

b.title: Prompt Loading of Implant-Backed Fixed Prostheses in Back Regions: A Systematic Exploration of Evidence

descriptions.problem: This work aims to estimate the best cases for a specific treatment to shorten the time it takes to fix a broken tooth in the back of the mouth, making it more efficient and cost-effective. It compares different approaches to find the most suitable ones.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a systematic search of existing studies to gather evidence, looking at data from various databases. They then manually reviewed the findings to identify the most effective cases.

descriptions.problem: The task is to evaluate the likelihood of successful long-term stability in a fixed restoration supported by anchoring elements in regions subject to high mechanical stress, based on available clinical and biomechanical records.
descriptions.approach: A structured review of published outcomes is conducted, filtering studies by design, duration, and follow-up, then comparing results across different anchoring strategies and patient profiles using standardized metrics.

a.title: Imidazoporphyrins as supramolecular tectons: synthesis and self-assembly of zinc 2-(4-pyridyl)-1 H -imidazo[4,5- b ]porphyrinate

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the ability of a certain type of molecule to assemble itself into a larger structure, and compares it to the same molecule in different states (solid vs solution). It also optimises the conditions for this assembly to occur.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a synthesis procedure to create the molecule, and then test its ability to self-assemble in two different environments. They compare the results to see if the conditions affect the assembly.

descriptions.problem: A system forms ordered structures through repeated interactions between molecules in both liquid and solid phases, with the arrangement depending on molecular shape and binding preferences.
descriptions.approach: Molecules link together via specific non-covalent interactions, forming predictable patterns. The structure emerges consistently under varying conditions, showing stability and reproducibility across environments.

b.title: The CX3CL1 oligomerization is required for efficient CX3CR1-specific cell adherence

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the structure and function of a protein complex that helps cells stick to the inner layer of blood vessels during an inflammatory response. It predicts how the protein complex behaves in different environments and optimizes its function.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use biochemical and biophysical methods to study the behavior of a specific part of the protein complex. They then use computer modeling to understand how the complex is assembled and how it affects cell behavior.

descriptions.problem: A system's ability to mediate binding between cells and a surface is assessed under varying conditions, with the strength of interaction measured across different structural configurations.
descriptions.approach: A structural component is tested for its tendency to form stable, cooperative assemblies in lipid-based environments versus random, non-cooperative forms, and its functional impact on binding is evaluated through controlled surface interactions.

a.title: Predicting the Presence and Abundance of Bacterial Taxa in Environmental Communities through Flow Cytometric Fingerprinting

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the presence and abundance of certain types of microorganisms in a community, using data from a variety of sources. It compares these estimates to data from other sources, such as observations of the community's behavior, to improve accuracy.
descriptions.approach: The research uses a combination of machine learning models to analyze data from a type of laboratory equipment that measures the size and properties of individual microorganisms. It follows a two-stage process: first, a model predicts whether a certain type of microorganism is present, and second, a model predicts how abundant it is.

descriptions.problem: The task is to estimate the presence and quantity of specific microbial groups in a mixed community based on physical and chemical traits measured in real-time across time.
descriptions.approach: A two-step model first determines whether a group is present using pattern recognition in measured traits, then estimates its relative quantity using statistical relationships derived from known trait-group associations.

b.title: Appendix: Animal Bones from Area B

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the number of animal bones found in a specific area, compares it to a known quantity, and optimizes a model to make a more accurate prediction. It uses data from various sources to support its findings.
descriptions.approach: The procedure involves collecting and analyzing data from different types of evidence, such as drawings and photographs, to make a more accurate estimate. The model is optimized through a process of comparison and refinement, using a team of experts and laborers to guide the process.

descriptions.problem: A pattern of material remains is analyzed to determine the relative abundance and distribution of different types of biological remains across a defined spatial region.
descriptions.approach: A grid-based sampling method is applied to group observations by location. Statistical clustering identifies recurring associations between types of remains and environmental contexts, enabling inference about past human activity and resource use.

a.title: Numerical data processing from a laser flash experiment on thin graphite layer

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the thermal properties of a thin, flat material attached to a material with known properties. It compares the material's thermal behavior to a theoretical model to make predictions about its thermal properties.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves collecting data from a series of high-energy events that cause the material to heat up quickly. The collected data is then used to solve a mathematical problem that describes how heat moves through the material.

descriptions.problem: A material's ability to transfer heat through a thin film attached to a conductive base is estimated from temperature measurements taken over time after a sudden heat input.
descriptions.approach: Temperature signals are fitted to a mathematical model of heat flow through three distinct regions. Parameters are adjusted to minimize the difference between predicted and observed temperature changes using iterative optimization.

b.title: Novel soluble and thermally stable polyimides derived from 4-(4-diphenylphosphino)phenyl-2,6-bis(4-aminophenyl)pyridine and various aromatic dianhydrides

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the thermal stability of a new material, comparing its properties to those of a standard material under various conditions. It predicts the material's performance in terms of its weight loss, residue, and glass transition temperature.
descriptions.approach: The researchers synthesized the material by combining two chemicals through a series of chemical reactions, then tested its properties by subjecting it to heat, flame, and mechanical stress.

descriptions.problem: A material is designed to maintain structural integrity under heat and mechanical stress, with properties such as solubility, flexibility, and resistance to flame being evaluated across multiple variants.
descriptions.approach: A series of compounds are synthesized by reacting a diamine precursor with diverse cyclic anhydride monomers, then heated to form cross-linked networks. Physical and thermal performance is assessed through controlled heating, mechanical testing, and solvent compatibility trials.

a.title: Qualitative and asymptotic analysis of repulsion systems with diverse applications

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the behavior of individual or cells under various mechanisms that push them apart, comparing the results to understand how these mechanisms affect their movement. It also predicts how these mechanisms will behave in different scenarios.
descriptions.approach: The researchers use a mathematical model to study the behavior of these mechanisms, following a procedure that involves analyzing different types of interactions between individual or cells, and comparing the results to understand the underlying mechanisms.

descriptions.problem: A system of interacting units is analyzed to understand how their collective behavior evolves over time under different interaction rules. The behavior is studied in both unconstrained and confined environments, focusing on how interactions influence long-term patterns and stability.
descriptions.approach: Units update their positions based on predefined interaction rules that depend on distance and relative orientation. The evolution is tracked over time, and patterns in movement and clustering are identified across different environmental constraints and interaction types.

b.title: Single-cell analysis reveals shared adaptive responses across different types of podocyte injury

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the molecular mechanisms underlying different types of damage to a crucial component of the glomerular filtration barrier, and identifies the shared adaptive responses of these damaged cells. It compares the effects of different types of damage on the same cells and explains the underlying disease mechanisms.
descriptions.approach: The researchers analyzed data from 16 samples of cells from healthy individuals and patients with different diseases, identifying 11 major cell types and analyzing their responses to damage. They used a combination of computational analysis and experimental validation to confirm their findings.

descriptions.problem: A system-wide response is inferred from cellular gene expression patterns across diverse disease conditions, identifying common molecular trajectories despite different initial triggers.
descriptions.approach: Cells are grouped by similar expression profiles, and dynamic changes in gene activity over time are mapped to detect shared adaptive phases, using high-resolution molecular data from individual cells.

a.title: DC-STGCN: Dual-Channel Based Graph Convolutional Networks for Network Traffic Forecasting

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future state of a complex system with many interconnected parts, using historical data to make predictions about its behavior over time. It aims to improve the accuracy of these predictions by capturing the relationships between the system's parts.
descriptions.approach: The model uses a combination of two main components: one extracts patterns in the system's behavior over time, and the other captures the relationships between the system's parts. It then uses these patterns to make predictions about the system's future state.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates future patterns in a dynamic process influenced by both repeating daily and weekly cycles, and spatial relationships among entities. It analyzes sequences of observations over time and across interconnected units to predict future values with high accuracy.
descriptions.approach: It splits the data into two temporal streams, each processed through a module that captures local and global relationships. A recurrent unit refines temporal patterns, while a dual-path mechanism separately models connectivity and proximity-based dependencies.

b.title: Advancing polar motion prediction with derivative information

descriptions.problem: This study aims to improve the accuracy of predicting the position of the Earth's axis over time, which is essential for various applications such as navigation and climate studies. It estimates the position of the axis based on historical data and optimizes the model to reduce the error.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of two methods: one that uses historical data to make predictions and another that uses a mathematical formula to analyze the patterns in the data. They tested this approach with different sets of data and compared the results to find the most accurate one.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the future values of two continuously changing variables based on past observations and their rates of change, aiming to improve accuracy in short-term predictions.
descriptions.approach: The model combines linear fitting with a statistical method that links current and past values of the variables and their rates of change, testing multiple input sets to determine which yields the most consistent and precise future estimates.

a.title: NCOA4 is a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with Immune Infiltrates in Glioblastoma

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between the expression levels of a protein and patient survival, and compares the survival rates of patients with varying levels of protein expression. It also aims to explain the underlying mechanisms and identify potential biomarkers for patient survival.
descriptions.approach: The study uses various computational tools to analyze data from a large dataset, including statistical tests, regression analysis, and network analysis. It follows a procedure of data collection, analysis, and model creation to identify patterns and relationships in the data.

descriptions.problem: A quantitative measure is estimated from patient data to predict survival outcomes based on the level of a specific gene's activity and its associations with immune system components.
descriptions.approach: A statistical model is built using patient records and gene expression levels, applying rank-based tests and survival analysis to link gene activity to survival time and immune component levels.

b.title: Clinicopathological significance of Kruppel-like factor 15 and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition related factors in bladder cancer

descriptions.problem: This research investigates the relationship between a specific gene and its role in a process that affects how cells change and move, and how this process is connected to the characteristics of tumors and patient outcomes. It aims to identify factors that can predict the likelihood of tumor recurrence and survival.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique to analyze tissue samples from patients, looking for the presence of specific proteins and their connections to other proteins. They also collected data on patient characteristics and outcomes, and used this data to identify patterns and make predictions about patient survival.

descriptions.problem: A system-wide pattern of protein activity is assessed to determine its relationship with disease progression and survival outcomes across a group of tissue samples.
descriptions.approach: Protein expression levels are measured in tissue samples and correlated with clinical outcomes. A statistical model identifies which protein interactions and expression levels independently predict survival and disease spread.

a.title: Homophily dynamics outweigh network topology in an extended Axelrod’s Cultural Dissemination Model

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of different network structures on the spread of cultural features in a group, comparing the outcomes of different models. It predicts how the structure of the group's relationships affects the spread of ideas over time.
descriptions.approach: The model uses a set of traits to define the features of the culture, and applies this to empirical data on people's attitudes. It tests different network structures and compares the results to see which has the most influence on the spread of ideas.

descriptions.problem: The evolution of group beliefs is studied based on interactions among individuals, using observed patterns from structured surveys. The outcome focuses on how shared traits spread and stabilize across a group, regardless of the specific connections between individuals.
descriptions.approach: Individuals update their beliefs by aligning with neighbors who share similar traits. The process runs over time, and results are compared across different connection patterns, showing that shared similarities dominate over structural links.

b.title: The construction of collective knowledge in a community of artisanal professional fishing women in the region of Guaraqueçaba - PR

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effectiveness of shared knowledge in empowering a community, compares it to traditional models, and explains how it is created through social interaction and shared communication codes.
descriptions.approach: The study uses a network mapping approach to visualize the relationships between people and non-human elements, and compares the observed knowledge creation model to a specific model, revealing similarities and differences.

descriptions.problem: A pattern of knowledge development is observed in a group of individuals who interact regularly and share practices through lived experiences. The process is analyzed to determine how information flows, transforms, and is preserved across interactions, comparing it to a known model of knowledge evolution.
descriptions.approach: Interactions among individuals and their tools, materials, and routines are mapped over time. The flow of information is tracked through observation and narrative, then compared to a structured model of knowledge progression.

a.title: Believing and Unbelieving in the Dunciad

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the relationship between human beliefs and the nature of the world, comparing and contrasting different ideas about the existence of unseen truth. It aims to explain how these ideas are connected to the power of creative expressions.
descriptions.approach: The approach involves analyzing and linking concepts from theology and creative expressions to understand their ambiguous position in relation to empirical phenomena.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how deeply a set of ideas is tied to external observations, by analyzing patterns in how they are interpreted across different contexts and compared to known empirical outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The system maps relationships between abstract concepts and observable phenomena, adjusting its interpretation based on consistency with known data and the coherence of connections across diverse interpretive frameworks.

b.title: Homophily dynamics outweigh network topology in an extended Axelrod’s Cultural Dissemination Model

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the impact of different network structures on the spread of cultural features in a group, comparing the outcomes of different models. It predicts how the structure of the group's relationships affects the spread of ideas over time.
descriptions.approach: The model uses a set of traits to define the features of the culture, and applies this to empirical data on people's attitudes. It tests different network structures and compares the results to see which has the most influence on the spread of ideas.

descriptions.problem: The evolution of group beliefs is studied based on interactions among individuals, using observed patterns from structured surveys. The outcome focuses on how shared traits spread and stabilize across a group, regardless of the specific connections between individuals.
descriptions.approach: Individuals update their beliefs by aligning with neighbors who share similar traits. The process runs over time, and results are compared across different connection patterns, showing that shared similarities dominate over structural links.

a.title: LSTM-Based Dynamic Frequency Prediction

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the future state of a system's stability, specifically the frequency at which it operates, based on historical data. It aims to predict this state to inform decisions about how to maintain stability.
descriptions.approach: The system uses a type of artificial neural network to make predictions. It processes data about the system's past behavior, including factors such as energy usage and grid capacity, to make a forecast.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates how a critical operational variable changes over time in response to sudden disturbances, using historical patterns and temporal dependencies to forecast future behavior under stress.
descriptions.approach: It analyzes past behavior at different time lags, identifies key influencing factors, and applies a model that learns long-term temporal patterns to generate accurate future estimates based on recent and delayed observations.

b.title: Advancing polar motion prediction with derivative information

descriptions.problem: This study aims to improve the accuracy of predicting the position of the Earth's axis over time, which is essential for various applications such as navigation and climate studies. It estimates the position of the axis based on historical data and optimizes the model to reduce the error.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of two methods: one that uses historical data to make predictions and another that uses a mathematical formula to analyze the patterns in the data. They tested this approach with different sets of data and compared the results to find the most accurate one.

descriptions.problem: A system estimates the future values of two continuously changing variables based on past observations and their rates of change, aiming to improve accuracy in short-term predictions.
descriptions.approach: The model combines linear fitting with a statistical method that links current and past values of the variables and their rates of change, testing multiple input sets to determine which yields the most consistent and precise future estimates.

a.title: Toxic effects of subchronic oral acetamiprid exposure in rats

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effects of exposure to a certain substance on the health of a specific group of living organisms over a prolonged period. It predicts the impact of varying doses of the substance on the organisms' health and compares the results to determine the most harmful dose.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of biochemical and physiological tests to evaluate the substance's effects. They measured various chemical markers and physical changes in the organisms' tissues and compared the results to determine the substance's impact on the organisms' health.

descriptions.problem: A repeated exposure to a chemical compound is assessed for its impact on metabolic and physiological balance, measuring changes in key biochemical markers and organ structure over time.
descriptions.approach: Exposure levels are gradually increased across a range of doses, and physiological responses are monitored through repeated sampling of bodily fluids and tissue analysis, with outcomes compared across dose groups to identify patterns of systemic stress and organ-specific responses.

b.title: The Impact of Carvedilol on Organ Index, Inflammatory Mediators, Oxidative Stress Parameters and Skin Markers in D-Galactose-Induced Aging Mice

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a certain substance on various biological markers in mice that have been induced to age prematurely. It aims to compare the impact of this substance on oxidative stress, skin aging, and cardiac hypertrophy in mice that have been aged with and without the substance.
descriptions.approach: The researchers divided the mice into six groups and gave them different combinations of the substance, vitamin C, and a control substance. They then measured various biological markers in the mice's hearts and skin tissues to compare the effects of the different groups.

descriptions.problem: A substance is evaluated for its effect on biological systems showing signs of deterioration over time, measuring changes in tissue structure, stress levels, and molecular markers of damage and repair across different treatment schedules.
descriptions.approach: Animals are exposed to a model of progressive decline, then treated either before or after the onset of decline. Tissue samples are analyzed for biochemical and structural changes, and outcomes are compared across treatment timing and control groups.

a.title: GENOMIC FINGERPRINTS OF ARACHIS HYPOGAEA L. NATURAL GERMPLASM AS REVEALED BY iPBS MARKERS

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the genetic diversity of a specific type of plant, comparing the genetic information of 21 samples collected from their natural habitats. The goal is to understand the genetic variation within this plant type.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a technique to analyze the genetic information of these samples, comparing the patterns of genetic material to identify similarities and differences. They then used a mathematical method to group the samples based on their genetic similarities.

descriptions.problem: A set of biological samples is analyzed to determine unique patterns of molecular presence or absence across individuals, with the goal of distinguishing between them based on shared and distinct features in their genetic material.
descriptions.approach: A series of targeted molecular tests are applied to each sample. Results are compiled into binary records. Similarity between samples is computed using a distance metric based on shared features, and clusters are formed using a hierarchical grouping method.

b.title: The First Report of Trichinella britovi in Armenia

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the presence of a certain type of parasite in various animal species in a specific geographic region, based on samples of muscle tissue. It compares the results to previous studies and identifies a new species.
descriptions.approach: The researchers collected muscle samples from five different animal species and tested them for the presence of the parasite using a specific laboratory technique. They then compared the results to previous studies and identified the new species based on the characteristics of the parasite found in the samples.

descriptions.problem: The presence and distribution of a parasitic nematode in wild mammals are estimated from biological tissue samples, using molecular detection to identify specific genetic markers.
descriptions.approach: Tissue samples are processed to extract genetic material, then amplified and analyzed using a multi-target detection method to identify the species based on sequence patterns in the DNA.

a.topic_name: Synthesis and pharmacology of benzodiazepine derivatives
a.title: Abstract 747: A new class of DNA alkylating indolino-benzodiazepine agents (BIAs) linked with a DNA binding moiety for use with antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs)

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new class of compounds that can damage a specific type of molecule in cells, and compares their effectiveness to a similar but less effective class of compounds. It also predicts that these new compounds can be used to improve the therapeutic index of a treatment.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a combination of structure-activity relationship studies and experiments to identify and modify compounds that can damage the target molecule. They then tested these modified compounds in various cell lines and found that they were highly effective.

descriptions.problem: A molecule is designed to bind selectively to a specific cellular target and deliver a cytotoxic payload to cells expressing that target, with potency and specificity tuned through structural modifications.
descriptions.approach: A scaffold is engineered to bind a target site with high affinity, and its structure is modified to enhance binding strength and stability. Linkage to a targeting agent is achieved through chemically defined connections, preserving activity while enabling selective delivery.

b.title: Nail drug delivery system a review

descriptions.problem: Estimate the effectiveness of a treatment for a condition that affects the outer layer of a person's body, and identify a way to improve the delivery of a substance to this layer. The substance is difficult to deliver due to the layer's hardness and the limited amount of substance that can pass through.
descriptions.approach: Use a combination of physical and chemical techniques to disrupt or enhance the reactivity of the outer layer, allowing for improved delivery of a substance. This can be achieved by using various methods to alter the layer's structure or properties.

descriptions.problem: A system is designed to deliver a therapeutic agent through a rigid, protective barrier that naturally resists transfer of the agent. The goal is to achieve a consistent and effective concentration of the agent within the barrier's internal structure, especially when the barrier is compromised or altered by external conditions.
descriptions.approach: The agent is introduced through physical or chemical modifications to the surface or structure of the barrier. These modifications enhance the agent's ability to enter the barrier's interior, with methods including surface disruption, energy-based stimulation, or formulation-based release mechanisms.

a.title: Learning in 3D: Adjusting and Assessing an Introductory Biology 3D Printing Project for Virtual Learning

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a 3D printing project in teaching students about the structure-function relationships of biological entities. It compares the results of different versions of the project, with and without hands-on manipulation, to assess their impact on learning outcomes.
descriptions.approach: The project involves three steps: researching a biological entity, designing a 3D printed learning aid, and presenting a learning module incorporating hands-on manipulation. The approach follows a procedure of designing, testing, and refining the project to improve learning outcomes.

descriptions.problem: A learning activity is designed to help learners connect the structural features of complex biological systems to their functional roles, using hands-on or digital representations.
descriptions.approach: Learners investigate a system, create a tangible or digital model to represent its components, and present their understanding through interactive manipulation or explanation to peers.

b.title: 3D Modeling/Printing of Female Reproductive Pathologies: Students Contribution to Pathology Education Through A Research Elective

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effectiveness of a new teaching method in a medical education setting, comparing the outcomes of students who used this method to those who did not. It aims to explain how this method can improve learning outcomes and student engagement.
descriptions.approach: The method uses a combination of interactive, annotated content and feedback from a subset of participants to evaluate its effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. It involves collecting and analyzing data from a survey and free-text feedback to inform the development of the teaching method.

descriptions.problem: A structured learning activity is designed to help learners connect visual observations of biological specimens with detailed, context-rich explanations, using interactive content and real-time feedback to reinforce understanding.
descriptions.approach: A sequence of annotated visual data is paired with targeted questions and explanatory narratives generated by an automated system. Learners engage with faculty and peer facilitators, and their responses to specific components are collected and analyzed to refine the experience iteratively.

a.title: Essential Amino Acids-Rich Diet Decreased Adipose Tissue Storage in Adult Mice: A Preliminary Histopathological Study

descriptions.problem: This work estimates the effect of a specific type of food on the body's fat storage and muscle mass in a certain animal model. It compares the results of two groups of animals, one that eats a standard food and one that eats a food rich in a certain type of nutrient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a procedure where they gave two groups of animals a standard food and a food rich in a certain type of nutrient, and then examined the changes in their body fat and muscle mass after a certain period of time.

descriptions.problem: A system is evaluated to determine how a specific nutritional input affects body fat distribution and metabolic activity in a living organism over a short period.
descriptions.approach: A controlled intervention is applied, and changes in fat cell size, hormone expression, and energy-burning capacity are measured through microscopic analysis of tissue samples and associated molecular markers.

b.title: Novel 4th-generation phytase improves broiler growth performance and reduces woody breast severity through modulation of muscle glucose uptake and metabolism

descriptions.problem: This research estimates the effect of a new enzyme supplement on the growth performance and meat quality of a certain type of animal, comparing the outcomes of three different treatment groups. It predicts the impact of the supplement on the animal's weight, muscle quality, and disease risk.
descriptions.approach: The researchers used a controlled experiment with 30 groups of animals, each with a different treatment. They measured the animals' weight, muscle quality, and disease risk, and compared the results to identify the effect of the supplement.

descriptions.problem: A biological intervention is evaluated for its effect on growth efficiency and muscle tissue quality in a living organism, comparing outcomes across different treatment levels and measuring changes in metabolic activity and tissue composition.
descriptions.approach: A model tracks metabolic flux in muscle tissue, measuring gene expression and enzyme activity linked to energy production and storage, then correlates these with physical performance and structural defects in muscle tissue.

a.title: Comprehensive dielectric performance of alternately doped BST multilayer films coated with strontium titanate thin layers

descriptions.problem: This work aims to improve the performance of a specific type of material used in energy storage and microwave applications. It estimates and compares the properties of this material under different conditions.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a new material by combining two other materials in a specific order and using a modified process. They then studied the material's structure and properties using various techniques, such as X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy.

descriptions.problem: A system's ability to store and release energy efficiently while minimizing unwanted energy loss is evaluated under varying electrical conditions and structural constraints.
descriptions.approach: A layered structure is engineered with controlled atomic substitutions and interface layers to balance conductivity, energy retention, and signal integrity across frequency ranges.

b.title: Hot extruded Al5SiC-graphite composites: Effect of graphite on microstructure, flexural, compressive and wear resistance behavior

descriptions.problem: This work investigates how adding a certain type of material to a mixture affects its properties. It estimates and compares the effects of this material on the mixture's strength, weight loss, and friction coefficient.
descriptions.approach: The researchers created a mixture by combining the material with a base material and then tested its properties. They used a process to shape the mixture into rods and analyzed its properties using various tests.

descriptions.problem: A material's resistance to deformation under load and its performance under sliding contact are evaluated across different reinforcement levels and processing conditions.
descriptions.approach: A continuous process shapes powder-based material into a dense form. The resulting structure's internal arrangement and performance under stress and wear are analyzed through repeated testing under controlled conditions.
